qualification: diagnostic record of failures and rejected hypotheses behind the trusted Remote-SSH row

findings.cause: Remote-SSH requires bash (NoBash); the guest has only initramfs BusyBox applets
LinuxPrereqs (exit 207): neither a glibc loader/libstdc++ discoverable by the server nor a musl loader; the static CLI itself runs

findings.case: Nix closure with glibc listed in buildEnv
findings.cause: buildEnv linked none of glibc's lib/, so the custom linker path did not exist; fixed with a dedicated vscode-server-sysroot link farm
the CLI downloads the server itself inside the guest; ServerUnexpectedExit after the guest download fails. The harness now stages the pinned server archive

findings.case: extension-driven scp of the CLI archive
findings.cause: the extension runs scp through a VS Code terminal; it never completed although the identical command run by hand succeeded. Not attributed; the harness stages archives instead
date/touch/chmod/ps/getconf missing (APK --no-scripts skipped the busybox applet trigger); the installer's port arithmetic then failed and the CLI bind was refused by Landlock (EACCES)

findings.case: reopening the same folder after cold restart
findings.cause: VS Code's persisted remote state under data/User and data/Machine suppresses it. Disabling persistent terminals/task reconnection did not help; clearing workspaceStorage alone did not help; clearing data/User and data/Machine did. The qualifying run keeps that state and proves the reconnect with a second folder after verifying the first session's files persisted
the exec-server installer always requests cli-alpine-<arch> on Linux (static musl CLI); it was not a getconf mis-detection as first reported

findings.case: 2026-11-15 rerun, Nix second session, window closed by the operator
findings.cause: the operator closed the isolated editor window 26 s after the remote connected (renderer sent terminate to the local extension host); not a guest, transport or Remote-SSH result
the batch was stopped mid-run; its isolated VS Code instance survived the harness and kept writing its temporary profile until it was terminated at 12:33

findings.case: 2026-11-15 rows with Copilot sign-in dialogs over the isolated editor
findings.cause: an empty VS Code 1.146 profile opens Copilot sign-in dialogs; the rows passed at 21-47 s to task output while the operator dismissed dialogs. The probe now sets chat.disableAIFeatures=true

findings.case: 2026-11-15 rows run concurrently by two agent sessions
findings.cause: a second session ran the Nix rows while this one ran the Alpine rows: two VMs and two isolated editors at once. One libkrun Nix run directory was also moved mid-run. Process listing in this environment shows only part of the host's processes (ps), so the overlap was found from file timestamps and pgrep; batches now take a shared lock

findings.case: 2026-11-15 Nix second session with the unsupported-glibc prompt left to the operator
findings.cause: the Nix server runs through the custom-glibc route, so the workbench asks whether to connect to an unsupported OS; Cancel/Esc reopens the window without the remote, while an unanswered prompt does not block the connection. On 2026-11-14, with nobody interacting, the same rows passed; on 2026-11-15, with the operator answering dialogs, three Nix second sessions connected but never ran the folder-open task. With Allow pre-recorded (remote.unsupportedConnectionChoice.ssh-remote+rsvm=true) all four rows passed at about 14.4 s per session. Which interaction suppressed the task in each failed run was not logged

the 2026-11-14 rows copied extensions from ~/.vscode/extensions and recorded only package.json hashes. Those package.json files are unchanged and every installed file of all three extensions equals the now-pinned VSIX content apart from VS Code's __metadata; this is consistency on 2026-11-15, not proof of the 2026-11-14 tree
